Mr. Mohammad Nazrul Islam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-record ------ For the Respondent

Principal, Pabna Cadet College, Pabna, Bangladesh and another ------ Appellants
Vs.
A.B.M Abdul Matin ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin, J: This appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and order dated November 19, 2001 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4869 of 2000 discharging the Rule obtained against the judgment and decree dated September 22, 1996 of the Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) and Artha Rin Adalat, Pabna in Other Class Appeal No. 199 of 1993 dismissing the same. The appeal was filed against the judgment and decree dated September 21, 1993 (inadvertently in the leave granting order it has been written September 4, 1993) of the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Pabna in Other Class Suit No. 28 of 1993 decreeing the same with costs. 

 5. The trial Court decreed the suit on the findings that the allegations brought against the plaintiff do not call for dismissal from service, that the inquiry that was held was not proper and the order of dismissal having been passed in the background of the said non-proper inquiry the same is illegal and the action of the authority is nothing but misuse of power, that the order of dismissal passed in respect of the plaintiff is uncalled for and that action of the authority demonstrates highhandedness in respect of a ‘ধার্মিক ও নিরিহ’ person. 

 6. The defendants went on appeal. The appellate Court dismissed the appeal on the finding that the trial Court has not committed any error of law in passing the, judgment and decree and as such no interference is called for. As against the judgment and decree of the appellate Court the defendants moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained Rule. The High Court Division discharged the Rule on, the findings that the suit as framed against the defendants is quite maintainable and that allegations brought against the plaintiff "have not been proved by any corroborative evidence" and finally the High Court Division observed that there was no error of law or failure of justice because of the judgment and decree passed by the Courts below. 

 7. Leave was obtained to consider the submission that under Section 3(2) of the Cadet College Ordinance, 1964 Pabna Cadet College being a body corporate capable of "sue and to be sued" in its own name, the High Court Division erred in not dismissing the suit since the College was not impleaded as a party in the suit and because of or as consequence thereof decree passed is in executable. 

 11. The plaintiff has filed the suit against the Principal of the Cadet College and the Chairman, of the Cadet College Council and Adjutant General. The suit so filed by the plaintiff was not against the Cadet College which is a body corporate in the light of the provision of Section 3(2) of the Ordinance. It is the contention of the appellant since the College has not been sued by the plaintiff who is an employee in the college the suit so filed was not maintainable in view of the provision of Section 3(2) of the Ordinance. The question as to whether a proceeding is maintainable when the legal entity and capable of being sued, as in the instant case the cadet College, has not been made a party in the proceeding. In the case of Mohammed Abdul Naim Vs. the Chairman, Board of Director, Sonali Bank, Head office and others (Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 298 of 1994, dismissed on April 6, 1995) it has been held "The petitioner was in the service of Sonali Bank and his cause of action is against his employer and not against his appointing authority or appellate authority. They are merely functionaries of his employer it is obligatory for him to make his employer a party to the application or else any decree in his favour will be in executable, his employer not being bound by the decree". The facts of the case was that petitioner was an employee of the Sonali Bank and he was dismissed from his service. His departmental appeal was also dismissed and thereupon he filed petition before the Administrative Tribunal and the same was allowed. Thereupon the Respondent went on appeal before. the Administrative Appellate Tribunal and the Administrative Appellate Tribunal set aside the judgment of the Administrative Tribunal upon observing that Sonali Bank itself is a legal entity and capable of being sued having not been made party to the case the petition before the Administrative Tribunal was not maintainable. Then the petitioner moved the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh by filing Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal and the same was dismissed on the observation as mentioned hereinbefore. It may be mentioned in the aforesaid case it was contended that the omission was only technical defect but the said contention was not accepted. Prior to the above case similar question came up for consideration before this Court in the case of Md. Arfan Ali Vs. Sonali Bank and others (Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 26 of 1992, disposed of on May 28, 1992). The said case was filed impleading an Assistant General Manager, Sonali Bank as defendant No.1 before the Administrative Tribunal. The petitioner did not implead Sonali Bank, the employer, as party to the petition. Before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal and application was filed seeking amendment of the petition by way of striking off Respondent No.1 the Assistant General Manager, Sonali Bank and for substituting Sonali Bank as Respondent No.1 in place of Assistant General Manager and the amendment was allowed but at the time of hearing of the appeal it was found; that the case was time barred because sonali Bank was substituted after one year and 4 months from the date of passing of the impugned order. 

 14. As stated hereinbefore as per provision of Section 3(2) of the Ordinance the cadet College was required to be sued for the vindication of the grievance of the plaintiff or in other words for the redress of the grievance of the plaintiff as against his order of dismissal from the service of the Cadet College, but the plaintiff instead of seeing the Cadet College filed the suit impleading the Principal of the Cadet College and the Chairman of the Cadet College Council. This being the position the contention of the appellant that the suit was not maintainable and as such the judgment and order of the High Court Division and the judgment and decree of the courts below were not legally sustainable and same is not executable against the Pabna Cadet College merits consideration. 

 16. Since the suit was filed upon impleading persons who have no legal entity to attend the grievance of the Respondent in the light of the decree obtained by him and in view of the provision of law as in Section 3(2) of the Ordinance plaintiff legally was not competent to initiate the suit upon impleading whom he filed the suit seeking relief as regard the order of dismissal passed in respect of him and as the plaintiff did not file the suit in the light of the provision of Section 3(2) of the Ordinance we are of the view that the suit so filed was not maintainable and the High Court Division as well as the courts below were in serious error in awarding relief to the plaintiff as against the order of dismissal from service in a suit which was not maintainable.
